STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from Abraham’s episode and prayer, which asks security for Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, and prosperity for his progeny.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.anchor: the security of Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, prosperity for his progeny

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.claim: Abraham also prayed for forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.anchor: forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.

THALABI:v10p224/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص عن النبي
THALABI:v10p224/r4.claim: The Prophet recites Abraham's prayer about those who follow him and Jesus' statement about God's authority to punish or forgive, then raises his hands and pleads for his community.
THALABI:v10p224/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول الله سبحانه في إبراهيم: فمن تبعني فإنه مني

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayers concern Makkah and his children settled there, showing Quraysh that their lives oppose his hopes while Muhammad and his followers fulfill them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The purpose is to make evident to the Quraysh that the whole life that they are leading is totally against the supplications and desires of Abraham (sws).

NAHHAS:v2p370/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p370/r8.claim: ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم means God forgives that person if he repents.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r8.anchor: ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم ) أي له إن تاب

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r5.claim: The idols ‘misled many’ by becoming the cause of people’s straying, though idols themselves cannot reason or act; Arabic similarly says a house has bewitched someone who came to love it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r5.anchor:
أي ضللوا بسببها، لأن الأصنام لا تعقل ولا تفعل شيئا، كما تقول قد
فتنتني هذه الدار.

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r6.claim: ‘Whoever disobeys me, You are forgiving and merciful’ means God forgives him if he repents and believes, not an unrepentant unbeliever.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r6.anchor:
أي فإنك غفور رحيم له إن تاب وإن آمن، لا أنه يقول إن من كفر فإن
الله غفور رحيم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r3.claim: Idols caused many people to go astray; whoever follows Abraham’s religion belongs to him, while God may forgive disobedience short of shirk.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r3.anchor: أي: ضلوا بسببها { فمن تبعني } على ديني

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r2.speaker: الجحدري، الثقفي، أبو الهجهاج
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r2.claim: They read وأجنبني with hamza; the author explains both جنبني and أجنبني as turning Abraham and his children away from worshipping idols, with the latter also suggesting making them devoted to God.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r2.anchor: قراءة الجحدري والثقفي وأبي الهجهاج: "وأجنبني"3 بقطع الألف

DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.claim: God answered Abraham’s prayer: none of his descendants worshiped idols after it, the town became safe and provisioned, and God made him a leader and guided his descendants to prayer, rites, and repentance.
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وإذ قال ابراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

DURR-FULL:v5p45/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r5.claim: The idols that misled many people are the idols themselves; Abraham’s reply models mercy rather than cursing, and Qatada condemns habitual cursing, citing Jesus’ prayer in 5:118.
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس} قال: الأصنام {فمن تبعني فإنه مني

DURR-FULL:v5p45/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed for any Arab who met God as a sincere believer affirming the meeting with Him, asking that God forgive him during his lifetime.
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r6.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إني دعوت للعرب

SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r1.claim: The pronouns in إنهن and أضللن refer to the idols, a non-rational broken plural treated as feminine singular.
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r1.anchor: والضمير في " إنهن " و " أضللن " عائد على الأصنام لأنها جمع تكسير غير عاقل.

SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r2.claim: مني means from my followers or party.

SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r3.claim: من عصاني is conditional, with من as nominative subject; فإنك غفور رحيم is its answer, with an omitted resumptive له.
SAMIN-DURR:14:36/r3.anchor: قوله: { ومن عصاني } شرط، ومحل " من " الرفع بالابتداء، والجواب

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n51/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n51/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n51/r1.claim: Abraham accepts God's verdict in 2:124 concerning sinners among his descendants.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n51/r1.anchor: Thus, Abraham accepts God's verdict (given in 2:124) regarding the sinners from among his descendants.

GHARNATI:v1p185/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
GHARNATI:v1p185/r1.claim: The Prophetic arrangement includes the seven long suras, the Hawamim, and the Mufassal; the rest may have been delegated to the community, and Abu Muhammad left that second category undecided.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r1.anchor: مما سوى ذلك يمكن أن يكون عليه السلام فوض فيه الأمر إلى الأمة بعده، ولم يقطع القاضى أبو محمد في هذا القسم الثاني بشىء

GHARNATI:v1p185/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r2.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p185/r2.claim: The apparent reports support most of Abu Muhammad's stated arrangement, though a few suras may have remained disputed or become disputed.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r2.anchor: وظواهر الآثار شاهدة بصحة ما ذهب إليه في أكثر ما نص عليه، ثم يبقى بعد قليل من السور يمكن فيها جري الخلاف أو يكون وقع

GHARNATI:v1p185/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r3.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p185/r3.claim: Because the issue rests on transmitted reports, disagreement by those unqualified to assess them is unsurprising.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r3.anchor: وإذا كان مستند المسألة النقل لم يصعب خلاف غير أهله

GHARNATI:v1p185/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p185/r4.claim: The coherence and connectedness required in the arrangement hold whichever position on its origin is adopted.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r4.anchor: على أن ما مهدناه من المراعاة في الترتيب حاصل لا محالة على كل قول

GHARNATI:v1p185/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r5.speaker: النبي
GHARNATI:v1p185/r5.claim: The Prophet's instruction to read al-Baqara and Aal Imran together as the two radiants supports their established sequence; the report is cited from Muslim and others.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r5.anchor: قوله عليه السلام: (اقرأوا الزهراوين: البقرة وآل عمران)

GHARNATI:v1p185/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r6.speaker: النبي
GHARNATI:v1p185/r6.claim: A report says that on the Resurrection the Quran and those who acted by it will come, preceded by al-Baqara and Aal Imran.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r6.anchor: وخرج أيضا قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: (يؤتى بالقرآن يوم القيامة وأهله الذين كانوا يعملون به تقدمه سورة البقرة وآل عمران.

GHARNATI:v1p185/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r7.speaker: معبد بن خالد
GHARNATI:v1p185/r7.claim: In a report in Ibn Abi Shayba's Musannaf, the Prophet prayed the seven long suras in one rakʿa and gathered the Mufassal in one rakʿa.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r7.anchor: وفي مصنف ابن أبى شيبة عن معبد بن خالد. قال: (صلى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالسبع الطوال في ركعة

GHARNATI:v1p185/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
GHARNATI:v1p185/r8.claim: Ibn Masud called Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta-Ha, and al-Anbiya among the early old suras and his treasured early material; the author notes he listed them in their settled order. The report is in Bukhari via Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r8.anchor: عبد الله بن مسعود يقول في بني إسرائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء: إنهن من العتاق الأولى، وهن من تلادى، فذكرها نسقا كما استقر ترتيبها.

GHARNATI:v1p185/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p185/r9.speaker: عائشة
GHARNATI:v1p185/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet's nightly bedtime practice included reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas in that sequence; Bukhari records the report.
GHARNATI:v1p185/r9.anchor: عن عائشة أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا أوى إلى فراشه كل ليلة جمع كفيه ثم نفث فيهما فقرأ فيهما

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham asks protection from idolatry for himself and his descendants; including himself shows how great the danger of polytheism is, since many have succumbed to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The second thing he requested in this supplication was to protect him and his progeny from the filth of idol worship.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: To convey the profound influence of idols, Abraham uses nouns and pronouns conventionally used for living beings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: when the purpose is to express the profundity of influence of something, the nouns and pronouns used are ones that are used for living beings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's words leave disobedient descendants who turned to polytheism to God's judgment, with mercy for those deserving it; Islahi stresses this is no prayer on behalf of polytheists.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It may be kept in mind that these words do not constitute any supplication from Abraham (sws) in favour of the polytheists.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

IBNHIBBAN:7235/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:7235/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:7235/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports that the Prophet recited Abraham’s plea and Jesus’ plea, prayed “My community,” and wept; God promised to satisfy him concerning his community and not grieve him.
IBNHIBBAN:7235/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول الله جل وعلا في إبراهيم

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r1.speaker: الكرماني
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r1.claim: Al-Kirmānī says the surah order is divinely fixed in the Preserved Tablet; the Prophet reviewed what he had gathered with Gabriel, twice in his final year, and al-Tibi agrees.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r1.anchor: وقال الكرماني في البرهان ترتيب السور هكذا هو عند الله تعالى في اللوح المحفوظ

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r2.speaker: ابن الحصار
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r2.claim: Ibn al-Hassar holds that both surah order and the placement of verses were established by revelation.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الحصار [ ترتيب السور ] و وضع الآيات موضعها انما كان بالوحي

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r3.speaker: البيهقي
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r3.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the Qur'an's surahs and verses already followed this order in the Prophet's time, except al-Anfal and Bara'a, as a later hadith indicates.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r3.anchor: وقال البيهقي في المدخل كان القرآن على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرتبا سوره وآياته على هذا الترتيبب إلا الأنفال وبراءة للحديث الآتي فيها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says many surahs had their order known in the Prophet's lifetime, including the seven long surahs, the hawamim, and al-Mufassal; the rest may have been left to the community.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r4.anchor: ومال ابن عطية إلى أن كثيرا من السور كان قد علم ترتيبها في حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم كالسبع الطوال والحواميم والمفصل

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the reports establish more than Ibn Atiyya allowed, leaving only a small remainder on which disagreement might be possible.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r5.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر بن الزبير الآثار تشهد بأكثر مما نص عليه ابن عطيه ويبقى منها القليل يمكن أن يجري فيه الخلاف

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r6.claim: As evidence that surah order was known, Ibn al-Zubayr cites the Prophet's instruction to read al-Zahrawayn, identified as al-Baqara and Al Imran; Muslim transmits it.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r6.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأوا الزهراوين والبقرة وآل عمران رواه مسلم

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r7.speaker: سعيد بن خالد
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr also cites Sa'id ibn Khalid's report that the Prophet recited the seven long surahs in one rak'a and grouped al-Mufassal in another.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r7.anchor: وكحديث سعيد بن خالد أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بالسبع الطوال في ركعة وأنه كان يجمع المفصل في ركعة

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r8.claim: Another cited report says the Prophet recited al-Ikhlas and the two refuge surahs when going to bed; al-Bukhari transmits it.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r8.anchor: وأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان اذا أوى إلى فراشه قرأ قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين أخرجه البخاري

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r9.claim: Ibn Mas'ud called al-Isra, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta Ha, and al-Anbiya among the earliest treasured surahs in his recitation legacy.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r9.anchor: وفيه عن ابن مسعود أنه قال في بني اسرائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء انهن من العتاق الأول وهن من تلادي

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas holds that the Prophet arranged the surahs, citing the report that he received the seven long surahs in place of the Torah, the Mathani in place of the Gospel, and al-Mufassal as a special gift.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r10.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر النحاس المختار أن تأليف السور على هذا الترتيب من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحديث أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطوال

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r11.speaker: ابن حجر
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r11.claim: Ibn Hajar says most surah ordering is fixed by prophetic instruction, citing Aws al-Thaqafi's report about the Prophet's division of the Qur'an into groups of three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, then al-Mufassal.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p69/r11.anchor: وقال الحافظ ابن حجر ترتيب معظم السور توقيفي لحديث أحمد وأبي داود عن أوس الثقفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.claim: After condemning Quraysh and other Arabs for replacing God's favor with disbelief and idols, the passage recalls their ancestor Abraham: he prayed for Mecca's safety and his descendants' avoidance of idols, then settled them by the House for prayer, contrasting their father's faith with their idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه تعالى لما ذكر التعجيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.claim: The repeated address to God is an appeal for compassion; Abraham explains his request by noting that he had seen his father and people worship idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.anchor: وكرر النداء استعطافا لربه تعالى، وذكر سبب طلبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r7.claim: The idols caused people to stray; the wording is like saying the world tempted them, meaning they were tempted and deluded because of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r7.anchor: ومعنى أضللنا: كنا سببا لإضلال كثير من الناس، والمعنى: أنهم ضلوا بعبادتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r9.claim: The feminine pronoun for idols treats a nonrational plural as feminine singular; the masculine plural in fa-qad ḍallū is a figurative agreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r9.anchor: وأنث الأصنام لأنه جمع ما لا يعقل يخبر عنه أخبار المؤنث كما تقول: الأجذاع انكسرت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r10.claim: Following Abraham means following his religion and teaching; “he is of me” expresses exceptionally close attachment and association.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r10.anchor: فمن تبعني أي: على ديني وما أنا عليه، فإنه مني. جعله لفرط الاختصاص به وملابسته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r1.claim: By analogy with the saying about fraud, being “not of us” means not among the qualities of believers; fraud is so grave that it threatens faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r1.anchor: كقوله: «من غشنا فليس منا» أي ليس بعض المؤمنين تنبيها على تعظيم الغش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r2.claim: The phrase forms a semantic antithesis, since following Abraham entails obeying him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r2.anchor: ومن عصاني، هذا فيه طباق معنوي، لأن التبعية طاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r3.claim: Muqatil understands disobedience here as persisting in shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: ومن عصاني فيحادون الشرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the plea to mean that God forgives past disobedience when the sinner turns from it and begins obeying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تغفر لي ما سلف من العصيان إذا بدا لي فيه واستحدث الطاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the parallel with following Abraham points to unbelief; forgiveness therefore means when they believe, phrased with Abraham’s refined courtesy, as in Jesus’ prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ومن عصاني ظاهره بالكفر لمعادلة قوله: فمن تبعني فإنه مني

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r6.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r6.claim: The Prophet likens Abu Bakr to Abraham, citing Abraham's statement in 14:36 about those who follow him and God's mercy toward those who disobey.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r6.anchor: وإن مثلك يا أبا بكر كمثل إبراهيم عليه السلام، قال: {من تبعني فإنه مني، ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم}

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the idols; their causing people to stray is figurative because they are inanimate, while God is the actual misleader.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r1.anchor: اي الاصنام ( اضللن كثيرا من الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r2.claim: The statement explains Abraham's preceding prayer, and the address “Lord” signals special concern and hope that the request will be answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r2.anchor: وهذا تعليل لدعائه عليه السلام السابق وصدر بالنداء إظهارا للاعتناء به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r3.claim: “From me” may be partitive by simile, making the follower like an inseparable part of Abraham, or connective, meaning attached to him in religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون ( من ) تبعيضية على التشبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r4.speaker: الشريفي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r4.claim: Al-Sharīf's commentary explains connective min as marking the follower's connection to Abraham rather than literal origin; al-Ālūsī favors a specific implied relation over a general one.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r4.anchor: كذا في حواشي شرح المفتاح للشريفي يعني أن مجرورها ليس مبدأ أو منشأ لنفس ما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r5.speaker: الجلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r5.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the connective min in “you are from me” has a specific understood relation, glossed as being connected to and deriving status from the speaker.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r5.anchor: كما قاله الجلال السيوطي في بيان الخبر من أن ( مني ) فيه خبر المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r6.claim: Following Abraham means following his call to monotheism and the religion of Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r6.anchor: منهم فيما أدعو إليه من التوحيد وملة الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r7.claim: “Disobeyed me” means did not follow Abraham; this wording implies he continued preaching, so nonfollowers failed through disobedience rather than lack of access to the message.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r7.anchor: والتعبير عنه بالعصيان كما قيل للايذان بأنه عليه السلام مستمر على الدعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r8.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r8.claim: Al-Baḥr notes a semantic antithesis between following Abraham and disobeying him, since following is obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235/r8.anchor: وفي البحر أن بين الاتباع والعصيان طباقا معنويا لأن الاتباع طاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r1.claim: Some commentators supply an omitted clause: “whoever disobeys me, I will not pray against him,” followed by Abraham's appeal to God's forgiveness and mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r1.anchor: وفي الكلام على ما أشار إليه البعض حذف والتقدير ومن عصاني فلا أدعو عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r2.claim: The verse indicates that forgiveness of shirk can be possible; al-Ālūsī cites al-Nawawī's account that it was permitted for earlier communities but barred in Islamic law.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r2.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أن الشرك يجوز أن يغفر ولا إشكال في ذلك بناء على ما قال النووي

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r3.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddī, among those who deny that any dispensation allowed forgiveness of shirk, takes the promise as applying after repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r3.anchor: فمنهم من ذهب إلى أن المراد غفور رحيم بعد التوبة ونسب ذلك إلى السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r4.claim: One report from Muqātil restricts “disobedience” to sins below shirk, though al-Ālūsī says this ignores the wording's unrestricted contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r4.anchor: ومنهم من ذهب إلى تقييد العصيان بما دون الشرك وغفل عما تقتضيه المعادلة وروي ذلك عن مقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r5.claim: Another report from Muqātil says a person persisting in unbelief may be forgiven by being moved from unbelief to faith and guided to what is right.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه أنه قال : إن المعنى ومن عصاني بإقامته على الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that God may spare a person who persists in shirk by delaying punishment; it compares this to God's forgiveness despite people's wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r6.anchor: ومنهم من قال : المعنى ومن لم يتبعني فيما أدعو إليه من التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r7.claim: Some take the statement literally and say Abraham spoke before learning that God does not forgive shirk; this is no fault, since reason allows it and a prophet need not know every revealed proof at once.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال : إن الكلام على ظاهره وكان ذلك منه عليه السلام قبل أن يعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the narrower readings and argues that the unrestricted phrase concerns intercession for major sinners before repentance; he then extends that precedent to the Prophet through the command to follow Abraham.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r8.anchor: والإمام لم يرتض أكثر هذه الأوجه وجعل هذا الكلام منه عليه السلام شفاعة في إسقاط العقاب عن أهل الكبائر قبل التوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī signals that al-Rāzī's intercession argument is unpersuasive and points readers to an earlier discussion for the relevant answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p235#2/r9.anchor: وهو كما ترى وقد مر لك ماينفعك في هذا المقام فتذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.claim: An objection asks how Abraham, protected from idolatry, could pray for protection, and how the prayer was answered when many descendants worshipped idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.anchor: فإن قيل: قد كان إبراهيم عليه السلام معصوما من عبادة الأصنام، فكيف يستقيم السؤال؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r1.claim: The wording attributes misguidance to idols while meaning people strayed because of them, an inversion like saying Satan frightens people through his allies in 3:175.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r1.anchor: وهذا هو المقلوب، نظيره قوله تعالى: {إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r2.claim: Another explanation ascribes misguidance to idols because they are its cause, like saying 'the world tempted me' because it caused the temptation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: نسب الإضلال إلى الأصنام لأنهن سبب فيه، كما يقول القائل: فتنتني الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r3.claim: Whoever follows Abraham belongs to his religious community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r3.anchor: {فمن تبعني فإنه مني} أي: من أهل ديني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r4.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the disobedient person referred to is one who later repents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r4.anchor: قال السدي: معناه: ومن عصاني ثم تاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r5.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says the disobedience meant is anything short of associating partners with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: ومن عصاني فيما دون الشرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r6.claim: Another view says Abraham spoke this before God informed him that He would not forgive associating partners with Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: قال ذلك قبل أن يعلمه الله أنه لا يغفر الشرك

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r1.claim: Abraham asks protection from the idols’ misguidance, attributing it to them causally as worldly life is said to have deluded people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r1.anchor: فلذلك سألت منك العصمة واستعذت بك من إضلالهن

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r2.claim: The causal attribution echoes the statement that worldly life deluded them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r3.claim: Whoever follows Abraham’s religion is of him, a part of him inseparable in religious matters.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r3.anchor: { فمن تبعنى } على ديني. { فإنه منى } أي بعضي لا ينفك في أمر الدين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r4.claim: God can forgive the disobedient from the outset or after enabling repentance; this supports that any sin, even shirk, may be forgiven, though the threat distinguishes it from other sins.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r4.anchor: تقدر أن تغفر له وترحمه ابتداء، أو بعد التوفيق للتوبة. وفيه دليل على أن كل ذنب فلله أن يغفره حتى الشرك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Mujāhid that a carved image shaped like a human is a ṣanam, while one carved in another shape is a waṯan.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r1.anchor: وما كان منحوتا على غير خلقة البشر فهو وثن - قاله الطبري عن مجاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm renews the address and omits the vocative particle to intensify his intimate appeal; the singular possessive keeps the utterance in one consistent pattern.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r2.anchor: تم بين زيادة الاهتمام بأمر الأصنام بإعادة النداء , وأسقط الأداة - زيادة في التملق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r3.claim: The attribution that the idols led people astray is figurative, with causation as its relation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r3.anchor: إسنادا مجازي علاقته السببية { كثيرا من الناس فمن

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r4.claim: As a consequence of Ibrāhīm's aversion to idols, whoever follows him in avoiding them belongs to his party, way, and religion, and he asks God to grant that person the promised success.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r4.anchor: أي من حزبي لكونه على طريقتي وديني , فأتني ما وعدتني فيه من الفوز

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r5.claim: The one who disobeys Ibrāhīm by going astray through idols deserves Hell; if God punishes him he remains God's servant, and if God forgives him, God has full discretion to do so.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r5.anchor: فضل بها فقد استحق النار , فإن عذبته فهو عبادك , وإن غفرت له فأنت لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r6.claim: Ghāfūr means abundant covering of sins and Raḥīm abundant honoring after that covering; the emphatic wording displays Ibrāhīm's heightened hope for pardon.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r6.anchor: أي بليغ الستر { رحيم * } أي بليغ الإكرام بعد ستر الذنوب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r7.claim: Ibrāhīm's request for forgiveness cannot diminish God's majesty or wisdom; al-Biqāʿī connects this to Jesus's prayer in al-Māʾidah.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r7.anchor: لأنه لا ينقص به شيء من عزته سبحانه ولا حكمته - كما أشار إليه دعاء عيسى عليه السلام في المائدة

BURSEVI:v4p282/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282/r1.claim: Idols caused people to stray as the occasion of misguidance, though they lack agency, just as worldly life causes people to be deceived.
BURSEVI:v4p282/r1.anchor: أي : الأصنام أضللن كثيرا من الناس ولذلك سألت منك أن تعصمني وبني

BURSEVI:v4p282/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p282/r2.claim: Some say devils entered idols and spoke through them: one in Abū Jahl’s idol slandered the Prophet, then the idol professed Islam and warned worshippers, so Abū Jahl smashed it and alleged sorcery.
BURSEVI:v4p282/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان الاضلال منهن لأن الشياطين كانت تدخل أجواف الأصنام وتتكلم كما حكى أن واحدا من الشياطين دخل جوف صنم أبي جهل

BURSEVI:v4p282/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282/r3.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v4p282/r3.claim: Kamal Khujandi’s couplet says breaking the idol of pride in the lovers’ religion is better than a hundred acts of worship.

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r1.claim: Min is partitive: a follower is like a part of Abraham, inseparable from him; likewise, a cheat is not one of the believers because cheating is not their trait.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r1.anchor: من تبعيضية فالكلام على التشبيه أي كبعضي في عدم الانفكاك عني

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r2.claim: Disobeying Abraham means not following him; it is set against following just as disbelief is set against gratitude by abandoning thanks.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r2.anchor: ومن عصاني أي لم يتبعني فإنه في مقابلة تبعني

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r3.claim: God can forgive and show mercy to the disobedient either from the outset or after repentance.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r3.anchor: قادر على أن تغفر له وترحمه ابتداء وبعد توبته

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r4.claim: In Ashʿarī theology every sin, even shirk, is rationally forgivable because punishment is God’s right, though scripture says He does not forgive shirk.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r4.anchor: وفي دليل على أن كل ذنب فلله تعالى أن يغفره حتى الشرك

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r5.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says Abraham preserves adab by saying who disobeys me, not who disobeys You; forgiving such a sinner displays exceptional generosity.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r5.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" قد حفظ الأدب فيما قال ومن عصاني

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r6.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r6.claim: A herald beneath the Throne says God pardoned claims owed to Him by Muhammad’s community; they must pardon one another’s remaining claims, then enter Paradise through His mercy.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r6.anchor: في الحديث : "ينادي مناد من تحت العرش يوم القيامة يا أمة محمد

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r7.claim: تبعات is the plural of تبعة, a right or claim owed to another.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r7.anchor: والتبعات جمع تبعة بكسر الباء ما اتبع به من الحق

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r8.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r8.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh says mercy is for sinners if reward is for the obedient; though not obedient, he hopes for reward, and as a sinner he hopes for mercy.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r8.anchor: وذكر أن يحيى بن معاذ الرازي رحمه الله قال إلهي إن كان ثوابك للمطيعين

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r9.claim: The accompanying Persian couplet urges the God-knower toward Paradise and calls sinners fitting recipients of divine generosity.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r9.anchor: نصيب ماست بهشت اي خداشناش برو كه مستحق كرامت كنا هكارانند

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r9.claim: Idols are said figuratively to mislead because they are occasions and causes of error; the actual creator of misguidance is God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r9.anchor: ونسب إلى الأصنام أنها أضلت كثيرا من الناس- تجوز-

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r10.claim: Another view takes the idols here to mean gold and silver coins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالأصنام هنا الدنانير والدراهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r11.claim: Disobeying Abraham apparently means unbelief, paired with following him; God's forgiveness is understood as accepting unbelievers' repentance until they believe, not forgiving disbelief as such.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r11.anchor: وقوله: ومن عصاني ظاهره بالكفر، بمعادلة قوله: فمن تبعني فإنه مني، وإذا كان ذلك كذلك فقوله: فإنك غفور رحيم معناه: بتوبتك على الكفرة حتى يؤمنوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r12.claim: Abraham uses a gracious formula because of his commitment to beautiful speech and refined courtesy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r12.anchor: لكنه حمله على هذه العبارة ما كان يأخذ نفسه به من القول الجميل والنطق الحسن وجميل الأدب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r13.claim: Qatāda says to notice Abraham's words: the prophets were not abusive or given to cursing; Jesus speaks similarly in 5:118.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: اسمعوا قول الخليل صلى الله عليه وسلم، والله ما كانوا طعانين ولا لعانين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet recited these verses, prayed for his community, and received good news about them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.anchor: وأسند الطبري عن عبد الله بن عمر حديثا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: تلا هاتين الآيتين ثم دعا لأمته،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r1.claim: Idols do not literally possess the power to mislead or act; people stray because of them, so they are figuratively said to have led people astray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r1.anchor: يعني الأصنام وهي لا توصف بالإضلال ولا بالفعل ولكنهم لما ضلوا بسببها كانت كأنها أضلتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r2.claim: Whoever follows Abraham follows the religion of monotheism and belongs to his community in faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ فمن تبعني ﴾ عل ديني التوحيد ﴿ فإنه مني ﴾ أي فهو على ملتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r3.claim: Al-Suddi understands the plea for forgiveness to concern a disobedient person who later repents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r3.anchor: أحدها ومن عصاني ثم تاب فانك غفور رحيم قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r4.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan limits this disobedience to sins short of associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r4.anchor: والثاني ومن عصاني فيما دون الشرك قاله مقاتل بن حيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r5.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman includes disbelief: God forgives by accepting repentance and guiding the person to monotheism.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r5.anchor: والثالث ومن عصاني فكفر فإنك غفور رحيم أن تتوب عليه فتهديه إلى التوحيد قاله مقاتل بن سليمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari suggests Abraham made this prayer before learning that God would not forgive idolatry, as when Abraham sought forgiveness for his father.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري يحتمل أن يكون دعا بهذا قبل أن يعلمه الله تعالى أنه لا يغفر الشرك كما استغفر لأبيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r5.claim: Abraham acknowledges that idols have led many people astray and disavows their worshippers, leaving their fate to God's will: He may punish or forgive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r5.anchor: وأنه برئ ممن عبدها، ورد أمرهم (2) إلى الله، إن شاء عذبهم (3) وإن شاء غفر لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r6.claim: The appeal to God's will does not suggest that forgiveness of idolaters will occur; it simply entrusts their case to Him, as in Jesus's words at 5:118.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r6.anchor: ليس في هذا أكثر من الرد إلى مشيئة الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr reports that the Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus's prayers, raised his hands weeping and repeated “My community” three times; God promised to satisfy him concerning his community and not grieve him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول إبراهيم: {رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r2.claim: The preceding claim that misguidance is not from God, together with this verse's account of following and disobedience, treats these as acts of the servant.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن العصيان والاتباع فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r8.claim: The idols are called misleaders because people went astray on their account, like saying that the world tempted or deceived people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r8.anchor: وإنما جعلن مضلات ؛ لأن الناس ضلوا بسببهن ، فكأنهن أضللنهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r9.claim: Following Abraham means sharing his upright Muslim faith; “he is of me” means intimate belonging.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r9.anchor: على ملتي وكان حنيفا مسلما مثلي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r10.claim: He compares “he is of me” with the prophetic saying “whoever cheats us is not one of us,” meaning fraud is not a believer's trait.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r10.anchor: وكذلك قوله : ( 573 ) ( من غشنا فليس منا ) أي ليس بعض المؤمنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r11.claim: God forgives the past disobedience of someone who changes course and begins obeying; another interpretation limits the disobedience to matters below idolatry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r11.anchor: تغفر له ما سلف منه من عصياني إذا بدا له فيه واستحدث الطاعة لي . وقيل : معناه

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r3.claim: The idols led many people astray through worshipping them.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r3.anchor: يعني أضللن بعبادتهن كثيرا من الناس

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r4.claim: Whoever follows Ibrahim follows his religion and belongs to his community.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r4.anchor: على ديني، { فإنه مني } على ملتي

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r5.claim: The one who disobeys Ibrahim is a disbeliever; God may forgive, lead the person to repent, and guide them to monotheism, as in 33:24.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r5.anchor: أن تتوب عليه، فتهديه إلى التوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.claim: The idols caused people to go astray: people strayed because of them, so the idols are spoken of as if they themselves led people astray.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.anchor: جعلن مضلات على طريق التسبيب لأن الناس ضلوا بسببهن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.claim: Whoever follows Abraham's religion as a sincere monotheist is of him, meaning like a part of him through their close bond.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ فمن تبعني ﴾ على ملتى وكان حنيفا مسلما مثلى ﴿ فإنه مني ﴾ أي هو بعضى لفرط اختصاصه بي

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.claim: If disobedience means anything short of associating partners with God, Abraham asks God to forgive that disobedient person.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ ومن عصانى ﴾ فيما دون الشرك ﴿ فإنك غفور رحيم ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, whoever disobeys by committing shirk is forgiven if he repents and believes.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.anchor: أو ومن عصانى عصيان شرك فإنك غفور رحيم ان تاب وآمن

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r8.claim: The idols are said figuratively to mislead many because they are the cause of misguidance, though inanimate objects cannot act.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r8.anchor: لما كانت سببا للإضلال أضاف الفعل إليهن مجازا فإن الأصنام جمادات لا تفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r9.claim: Following Abraham means following the oneness of God; such a follower belongs to his religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r9.anchor: في التوحيد. { فإنه مني } أي من أهل ديني

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r10.claim: Disobeying Abraham here means persisting in associating partners with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r10.anchor: { ومن عصاني } أي أصر على الشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r11.claim: One view says Abraham made this prayer before learning that God does not forgive associating partners with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r11.anchor: قيل: قال هذا قبل أن يعرفه الله أن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r12.claim: Another view limits the forgiveness to those who repent of disobedience before death.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r12.anchor: وقيل: غفور رحيم لمن تاب من معصيته قبل الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r13.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r13.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the disobedience meant here is anything short of associating partners with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r13.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان: «ومن عصاني» فيما دون الشرك

QASHANI:14:35-38/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r4.claim: The idols mislead many by attachment and attraction to them, veiling people from unity.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r4.anchor: بالتعلق بها، والانجذاب إليها، والاحتجاب بها عن الوحدة

QASHANI:14:35-38/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r5.claim: Those who follow the spirit along the path of tawhid belong to it.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r5.anchor: في سلوك طريق التوحيد { فإنه مني ومن عصاني

QASHANI:14:35-38/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r6.claim: God’s forgiveness covers the disobedient person’s dark state with His light, and His mercy grants perfection after forgiveness.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r6.anchor: تستر عنه تلك الهيئة المظلمة بنورك { رحيم } ترحمه بإفاضة الكمال عليه

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r5.claim: Another answer limits the prayer to believing descendants: those who do not follow Abraham's religion are not of him, as Noah's son was not of his family in Qur'an 11:46.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r5.anchor: أن هذا الدعاء مختص بالمؤمنين من أولاده والدليل عليه أنه قال في آخر الآية : { فمن تبعني فإنه مني }

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r9.claim: All theological schools agree that attributing misguidance to idols is metaphorical, because inanimate things cannot act; people go astray through worshipping them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r9.anchor: واتفق كل الفرق على أن قوله : { أضللن } مجاز لأنها جمادات ، والجماد لا يفعل شيئا ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r1.claim: Whoever follows Abraham in religion and belief is “of him,” as close as a part of him; whoever disobeys him outside religion is entrusted to God's forgiveness and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r1.anchor: يعني من تبعني في ديني واعتقادي فإنه مني ، أي جار مجرى بعضي

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r2.claim: Razi argues that Abraham's request for forgiveness is intercession for major sinners among his community; its wording explicitly asks forgiveness and mercy for disobedient people.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r2.anchor: أن قوله : { ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم } صريح في طلب المغفرة والرحمة لأولئك العصاة

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r3.claim: The sinners cannot be unbelievers: Abraham had disavowed idolaters in his opening prayer, and “whoever follows me” implies nonfollowers are outside his religious community; the community agrees kufr's punishment cannot be removed by intercession.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r3.anchor: أنه عليه السلام بين في مقدمة هذه الآية أنه مبرأ عن الكفار وهو قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام }

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r4.claim: The wording is unrestricted, so it cannot be narrowed to minor sins; minor sins and major sins after repentance are already obligatorily forgiven according to his opponents.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r4.anchor: لأن قوله : { ومن عصاني } اللفظ فيه مطلق فتخصيصه بالصغيرة عدول عن الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r5.claim: Razi concludes that the verse establishes intercession removing the punishment of major sins before repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r5.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآية شفاعة في إسقاط العقاب عن أهل الكبائر قبل التوبة

RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r6.claim: If Abraham had this station, Muhammad must have it: no distinction is recognized, its absence would diminish Muhammad, and Muhammad was commanded to follow Abraham (Qur'an 6:90; 16:123).
RAZI-FULL:v19p105#2/r6.anchor: أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمور بالاقتداء بإبراهيم عليه السلام لقوله تعالى : { أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده }

RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r1.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the phrase means whoever disobeyed Abraham and then repented; Razi rejects this restriction because it was already refuted.
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r1.anchor: قال السدي معناه : ومن عصاني ثم تاب

RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r2.claim: One view says Abraham made this prayer before learning that God does not forgive associating partners; Razi rejects it because the context excludes intercession for disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الدعاء إنما كان قبل أن يعلم أن الله تعالى لا يغفر الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r3.claim: Another view says God is forgiving and merciful by transferring a person from disbelief to Islam; Razi objects that forgiveness and mercy imply dropping punishment, not conversion to faith.
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r3.anchor: وقيل من عصاني بإقامته على الكفر فإنك غفور رحيم

RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r4.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r4.claim: A further view takes forgiveness and mercy to mean delaying punishment or death until sinners can repent; Razi rejects it because contemporary unbelievers are neither punished immediately nor regarded by Muslims as forgiven.
RAZI-FULL:v19p106/r4.anchor: وأما الرابع : وهو أن تحمل المغفرة والرحمة على تعجيل العقاب أو ترك تعجيل الإمانة فنقول هذا باطل

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r8.claim: The follower is of Abraham because he agrees with him and belongs to his religious community.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r8.anchor: { فإنه منى } : أي موافق لي ومن أهل ملتي

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r9.claim: The one who disobeys Abraham opposes him and disobeys God.

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r10.claim: By saying God is forgiving and merciful, Abraham allusively asks Him to show mercy to those who disobeyed.

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r11.claim: Abraham says ‘who disobeys me,’ rather than ‘who disobeys You,’ because he seeks mercy for those who violated his own right and meets them with mercy instead of vengeance.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r11.anchor: ولم يقل : من عصاك ، وإن كان من عصاه فقد عصى الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r12.claim: The Prophet’s prayer for his people is fuller in pardon because he directly asks God to forgive them, saying they do not know.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r12.anchor: ويقال إن قول نبينا في هذا الباب أتم في معنى العفو حيث قال

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r13.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r13.claim: The Prophet prayed, ‘O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.’
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r13.anchor: حيث قال : ( اللهم اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون )

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r14.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r14.claim: Another reading says Abraham avoids making a definite request, maintaining the etiquette of supplication by stating God’s mercy instead.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r14.anchor: ويقال لم يجزم السؤال لأنه بدعاء الأدب

STUDYQURAN:14:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r1.claim: The claim that idols led people astray is figurative: people were misguided through serving lifeless idols.
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r1.anchor: is a figurative expression used to indicate the manner in which people have been misguided in their service to lifeless idols

STUDYQURAN:14:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r2.claim: Following Abraham means believing in God's Oneness and belonging to his monotheistic creed.
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r2.anchor: whoever follows Abraham in believing in God’s Oneness belongs to his monotheistic creed

STUDYQURAN:14:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r3.claim: The verse teaches that God forgives every sin except associating partners with Him, as stated in 4:48 and 4:116.
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r3.anchor: teaching that any sin will be forgiven by God except for the ascription of partners unto Him

STUDYQURAN:14:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r4.claim: Some commentators include shirk in the forgiveness Abraham asks for, understanding this as before God informed him that shirk is unforgiven.
STUDYQURAN:14:36/r4.anchor: According to some commentators, would then pertain to the time before God informed Abraham

TAB-FULL:v13p688/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p688/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p688/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the things that led people astray as the idols, glossing them as both awthān and aṣnām.
TAB-FULL:v13p688/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: {إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس} [إبراهيم: 36] قال: «الأصنام»

TAB-FULL:v13p689/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r1.claim: Whoever follows Abraham's faith, worships God alone, and abandons idols belongs to him by following his way and deeds.
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r1.anchor: {فمن تبعني فإنه مني، ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم} [إبراهيم: 36]

TAB-FULL:v13p689/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r2.claim: God forgives sinners and is merciful to His servants, pardoning whom He wills, including those who reject Abraham's call and associate partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r2.anchor: فإنه غفور لذنوب المذنبين الخطائين بفضلك، رحيم بعبادك، تعفو عمن تشاء منهم، كما:

TAB-FULL:v13p689/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r3.claim: Qatāda urges listeners to attend to Abraham's gentle prayer; prophets were not abusive cursers, a practice condemned as among the worst qualities, as Jesus likewise prayed about his people.
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r3.anchor: اسمعوا إلى قول خليل الله إبراهيم، لا والله ما كانوا طعانين ولا لعانين

TAB-FULL:v13p689/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r4.speaker: محمد
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r4.claim: The Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus' prayers, raised his hands weeping for his community, and God promised through Gabriel to please him and not grieve him over them.
TAB-FULL:v13p689/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول إبراهيم

SULAMI:v1p347#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p347#2/r1.claim: Some say Abraham did not curse those who disobeyed him; he named God's forgiveness and mercy, acknowledging that he had no claim over God's servants.
SULAMI:v1p347#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : لما هرب الخليل في استرزاقه للمؤمنين

TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r4.claim: Abraham calls his followers part of himself and says nothing comparable about others, which the author reads as disowning them; this supports restricting the community to the faithful line.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r4.anchor: حيث أتى بفاء التفريع وأثبت من تبعه جزءا من نفسه وسكت عن غيرهم كأنه ينكرهم ولا يعرفهم

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r4.claim: Repeating “My Lord” appeals to divine mercy; the idols' having led many astray explains why Abraham asks to be kept and his descendants kept from worshipping them.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r4.anchor: وقد أعاد النداء " رب " إثارة للرحمة الإلهية

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r5.claim: Misguidance is attributed to the idols through their association with the error, not because the idols act consciously; effects need not involve awareness in their cause.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r5.anchor: ونسبة الإضلال إلى الأصنام لمكان الربط الذي بين الضلال وبينهن وإن لم يكن ارتباطا شعوريا وليس من اللازم في نسبة أي فعل أو أثر إلى شيء أن يقوم به قياما شعوريا

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r6.claim: The conditional clause follows from the preceding division: people fall into those led from God's monotheistic path and those who offer themselves to God's protection.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r6.anchor: افترقنا نحن والناس طائفتين الضالون عن طريق توحيدك والعارضون لأنفسهم على حفظك وإجنابك

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r7.claim: Following Abraham means taking a path—his religion and way of life—not merely affirming God's oneness; the paired language of following and being led astray also evokes a path.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r7.anchor: والاتباع إنما يكون في طريق - وقد لوح إلى الطريق أيضا بقوله " أضللن "

TABATABAI:14:36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r1.claim: Following Abraham means adopting his whole path in belief and practice; disobedience means abandoning all or part of his way and law.
TABATABAI:14:36/r1.anchor: فمراده باتباعه سلوك طريقه والتدين بجميع ما أتى به من الاعتقاد والعمل وبعصيانه ترك سيرته وما أتى به من الشريعة اعتقادا وعملا

TABATABAI:14:36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r2.claim: The clause interprets “my sons” by extending Abraham's affiliation to later followers and excluding disobedient descendants; this resembles his prayer for the town's provision, later limited to believers and then extended to disbelievers temporarily.
TABATABAI:14:36/r2.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أولا أن قوله عليه السلام { فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم } تفسير لقوله

TABATABAI:14:36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r3.claim: The true heirs of Abraham include those who followed him, along with the Prophet and believers, as 3:68 states.
TABATABAI:14:36/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا

TABATABAI:14:36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r4.claim: Abraham may be adopting every follower and disowning any disobedient person, even a biological descendant; alternatively, he may affirm followers' affiliation while remaining silent about others, since silence is not explicit denial.
TABATABAI:14:36/r4.anchor: أن من الممكن أن يستفاد من قوله عليه السلام فيمن تبعه

TABATABAI:14:36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r5.claim: There is no problem with spiritual affiliation extending or narrowing natural descent: neither nations nor Islam treat birth alone as decisive, and the Qur'an says of Noah's son, “he is not of your family.”
TABATABAI:14:36/r5.anchor: ولا إشكال في ذلك بعد ظهور الدليل فإن الولادة الطبيعية لا يجب أن تكون هي الملاك في النسب إثباتا ونفيا

TABATABAI:14:36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36/r6.claim: Abraham does not claim the disobedient as his own or include them in his protection, leaving them to God's forgiveness and mercy.
TABATABAI:14:36/r6.anchor: ومن عصاني بترك طريقتي كلها أو بعضها سواء كان من بني أو غيرهم فلا ألحقه بنفسي ولا أسألك إجنابه وإبعاده بل أخلي بينه وبين مغفرتك ورحمتك

TABATABAI:14:36#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#2/r1.claim: The implied plea for mercy does not concern associating partners with God: God does not forgive shirk, though He may forgive lesser sins for whom He wills.
TABATABAI:14:36#2/r1.anchor: وليس المراد به نفس الشرك بالله حتى ينافي سؤال المغفرة كما قال تعالى إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r4.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r4.claim: Commentators object that Abraham’s words appear to request forgiveness for polytheists, although scripture says God does not forgive association with Him.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r4.anchor: ثم استشكلوا في قوله عليه السلام { ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم } من حيث اشتماله على طلب المغفرة للمشركين

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r5.claim: One answer says polytheism could be forgiven under earlier dispensations, and only this dispensation prohibited such forgiveness.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r5.anchor: وقد قيل في الجواب عن الإشكال أن الشرك كان جائز المغفرة في الشرائع السابقة وإنما رفع ذلك في هذه الشريعة

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r6.claim: Another answer supplies an unspoken condition: God is forgiving to the one who disobeys Abraham after that person repents.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r6.anchor: وقيل إن المراد ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم له بعد توبته ففي الكلام قيد محذوف

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r7.claim: A third answer reads the request as asking God to forgive and show mercy by bringing a persistently idolatrous disobedient person into monotheism.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ومن عصاني وأقام على الشرك فإنك غفور رحيم بأن تنقله من الشرك إلى التوحيد

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r8.claim: A fourth answer takes forgiveness as concealing the idolatry in this world and mercy as delaying immediate punishment.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمغفرة والرحمة الستر على الشرك في الدنيا والرحمة بعدم معاجلة العقاب

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r9.claim: A fifth answer keeps the wording literal and says Abraham spoke before learning that God would not forgive association; such knowledge could come later.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r9.anchor: وقيل إن الكلام على ظاهره وكان ذلك منه عليه السلام قبل أن يعلم أن الله لا يغفر الشرك

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r10.claim: A sixth answer limits the disobedience here to sins short of polytheism.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r10.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمعصية ما دون الشرك

TABATABAI:14:36#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r1.claim: The earlier-law explanation lacks evidence and is contradicted by warnings to Adam’s community and Jesus’ dispensation; Qur’anic judgment, afterlife, intercession, and prophetic prayers show no rescue from shirk except repentance before death.
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r1.anchor: دعوى كون الشرك جائز المغفرة في الشرائع السابقة دعوى لا دليل عليها بل الدليل على خلافها

TABATABAI:14:36#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r2.claim: Adding repentance without a textual qualifier is unwarranted and breaks the contrast: a repentant disobedient person rejoins Abraham’s followers, leaving the comparison one-sided.
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r2.anchor: تقييد المغفرة والرحمة بالتوبة تقييد من غير مقيد

TABATABAI:14:36#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r3.claim: The conversion and worldly-concealment readings depart from the apparent request: forgiveness is sought while disobedience persists and normally removes sin’s consequences, especially in the afterlife.
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r3.anchor: ظاهر طلب المغفرة للعاصي أن يغفر الله له حينما هو عاص لا أن يغفر الله له بعد خروجه

TABATABAI:14:36#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r4.claim: He calls the ignorance explanation especially implausible: late in life Abraham could not have been ignorant of basic doctrine, interceded without permission, and had God quote uncorrected nonsense; God explicitly justified his earlier prayer for his father by a prior promise.
TABATABAI:14:36#4/r4.anchor: أن يجهل ما هو من واضحات المعارف الدينية ثم يجري على جهله

TABATABAI:14:37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37/r1.claim: Restricting disobedience to lesser sins has no textual qualifier, unless reconstructed along lines already explained.
TABATABAI:14:37/r1.anchor: تقييد المعصية بما دون الشرك تقييد من غير مقيد

TABATABAI:14:37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37/r2.claim: The exegetes’ difficulties stem from neglecting what divine protection from shirk means and how the follower-belongs-to-me clause follows from the preceding prayer.
TABATABAI:14:37/r2.anchor: وقد وقعوا فيما وقعوا لإهمالهم تحقيق القول في معنى حفظه تعالى عن الشرك

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r3.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Abū ʿUbayda that al-Ṣādiq said whoever loves the Imams is of the Ahl al-Bayt, citing Abraham’s “whoever follows me belongs to me.”
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r3.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي عبيدة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من أحبنا فهو منا أهل البيت

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r4.claim: A second al-ʿAyyāshī report has al-Ṣādiq say that those among the audience who fear God and act righteously are of the Ahl al-Bayt; he and ʿUmar ibn Yazīd affirm their inclusion among Muḥammad’s family by reference to Abraham’s words and 3:68.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r4.anchor: وفيه عن محمد الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من اتقى الله منكم وأصلح

TABRISI:14:37#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r11.claim: The idols are said to have led people astray because people went astray through worshipping them, as one says a woman beguiled me when one became infatuated with her.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r11.anchor: معناه ضل بسببهن وعبادتهن كثير من الناس كما يقال فتنتني فلانة يعني افتتنت بحبها

TABRISI:14:37#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r12.claim: The poet's example means the man's camel wandered, not that someone intended to make it wander.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r12.anchor: هبوني امرأ منكم أضل بعيره له ذمة إن الذمام كبير

TABRISI:14:37#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r13.claim: Among the descendants settled there, whoever follows Ibrahim's monotheism and abandons idol worship belongs to his community and shares his state.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r13.anchor: يريد فمن تبعني من ذريتي الذين أسكنتهم هذا البلد على ديني في عبادة الله وحده

TABRISI:14:37#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r14.claim: God covers servants' sins and is merciful to them in all states, granting them favor.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r14.anchor: أي ساتر على العباد معاصيهم رحيم بهم في جميع أحوالهم

THALABI:v5p321/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p321/r5.claim: Attributing misguidance to idols describes an effect by its instrument, like Satan frightening people through his allies.
THALABI:v5p321/r5.anchor: يعني ضل بهن كثير من الناس عن طريق الهدى حتى عبدوهن وهذا من المغلوب

THALABI:v5p321/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p321/r6.claim: Whoever follows Abraham belongs to his religion and way.
THALABI:v5p321/r6.anchor: فمن تبعني فإنه مني على ديني وملتي

THALABI:v5p321/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r7.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v5p321/r7.claim: Al-Suddi understands the disobedient person as one who later repents.
THALABI:v5p321/r7.anchor: قال السدي: معناه ومن عصاني فتاب

THALABI:v5p321/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v5p321/r8.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says this refers to disobedience in matters short of shirk.
THALABI:v5p321/r8.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان: ومن عصاني فيما دون الشرك

THALABI:v5p321/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v5p321/r9.claim: The Prophet recited Abraham's words about followers and disobedient people and Jesus' plea about those he is asked to punish; he wept for his community, and God promised to satisfy him about them.
THALABI:v5p321/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول إبراهيم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#4/r1.claim: The idols caused many people to go astray, or many went astray through them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#4/r1.anchor: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس} أي: ضل بهن كثير من الناس.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq and others say people went astray because of the idols; since idols cannot reason or act, the deed is attributed to them as to a house that captivates someone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق وغيره: أي ضلوا بسببها؛ لأن الأصنام لا تعقل ولا تفعل شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says following Ibrahim means following his religion of monotheism and knowledge of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد على ديني بالتوحيد لك والمعرفة بك (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains he is of me as belonging to those who follow my religion and adhere to my covenant, as in the cited poem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: يريد من المتدينين بميني المتمسكين بحبلي؛ كما قال (¬2):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r4.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r4.claim: The poem's speaker says he is not one of a person who attempts immorality among Asad, meaning he does not adhere to that person's covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r4.anchor: إذا حاولت في أسد فجورا ... فإني لست منك ولست مني (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the disobedient person is forgiven if he repents and believes; Ibrahim is not saying God forgives someone who persists in unbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r5.anchor: قال السدي: معناه ومن عصاني ثم تاب (¬5)، {فإنك غفور رحيم}] (¬6) له إن تاب وإن آمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r6.claim: Muqatil restricts the disobedience to matters below polytheism; Abu Bakr explains it as violating some religious laws while affirming monotheism, for which a Muslim may be forgiven if God wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ومن عصاني فيما دون الشرك فإنك غفور رحيم (¬7)، وشرح أبو بكر هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r7.claim: Abu Bakr offers the possibility that the prayer preceded God's informing Ibrahim that shirk would not be forgiven; Ibrahim later disavowed his parents after learning they would not be forgiven.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p484/r8.claim: Another Abu Bakr explanation takes the disobedient person as persisting in unbelief; God is able to forgive by transferring him from unbelief to Islam and guiding him.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.claim: The account presents Abraham's grateful devotion and supplication as an example of servitude to God, and points to salvation through his monotheistic way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.anchor: Ayrıca Allah’ın verdiği sayısız ve sınırsız nimetlerin şükrünü yerine getiren bir kulun yani Hz. İbrâhim’in Allah’a karşı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r6.claim: Abraham counts believers protected from the means of shirk as members of his religion and among the saved.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r6.anchor: İbrâhim aleyhisselâm bu şirk vasıtalarından korunan müminleri kendi dininin mensuplarından ve kurtuluşa erenlerden saymış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r7.claim: For those who oppose him, Abraham entrusts the matter to God's forgiveness, displaying deep compassion and mercy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r7.anchor: kendisine karşı gelip isyan edenler hakkında ise, “Sen çok bağışlayan, pek esirgeyensin” diyerek onları Allah’ın af ve bağışına havale etmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.claim: Commentators say Abraham made the prayer in these verses after Mecca had become a settlement and he and Ishmael had built the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre İbrâhim bu âyetlerde bildirilen duasını da Mekke yerleşim merkezi haline geldikten ve İsmâil ile birlikte Kâbe’yi inşa ettikten sonra yapmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r17.speaker: author
